You break ground behind the hall — bed 1 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.

"Hey." A man, maybe 30s settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to." (Talk to A man, maybe 30s.)
Recipe: Bark armor (Level 1). You have seen bark armor. Plates of bark laced together, worn like a shell.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
A cold snap. Breath smokes. The woods go quiet.
⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.

Oussama and Benjamin lingered over the fire together.
Leo and Benjamin lingered over the fire together.

— DAY 2 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
🔥 “I don’t say this lightly.” Benjamin sets their bowl down. “Mia, your past story isn’t true, is it? I’ve heard enough versions now.” Nobody looks at Mia. Everybody does.

Mia is quiet for a long moment. Then, all in a rush: “Fine. It’s true. Not Denver — Stockholm, Sweden. I lied because the truth felt small.” The admission hangs there, and the village — to its credit — doesn’t pounce.
People bring you their suspicions, written down. You keep every one.
Snow by morning. Your breath comes out in ghosts.
A person, maybe 20s will work the garden once each day while at Haven. Other orders take priority.
You step into the Haven hall.

(Talking costs a little energy — 10 kcal a conversation. Small talk is cheap; going deep costs time, not more food.)
